newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-KONG SURVIVES TO MEET SAMSONOV.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-KONG SURVIVES TO MEET SAMSONOV.

text.p: Olympic champion Kong Linghui survived a five-game struggle against fellow Chinese Ma Wenge to set up a world championship semifinal later on Sunday against the rising star of men's table tennis, Vladimir Samsonov of Belarus.
Kong, the world number one, stayed on course to retain his title by eventually seeing off Ma 16-21 22-20 14-21 21-15 21-12.
That put him into what could be a gripping semifinal against Samsonov, the talented Belarussian.
The lanky 21-year-old from Minsk, already seeded joint third, shredded the resistance of a rival considered to be the premier defensive player in the world, Ding Song of China.
Not even Ding could contain the powerful forehand smash of Samsonov who won with surprising ease 21-13 21-9 21-10.

Sweden's 1989 world champion and second seed, Jan-Ove Waldner, sustained his bid for a repeat success, his speed of reaction and quick backhand flicks helping him past 1993 champion Jean-Philippe Gatien of France 21-7 22-20 21-14.
"Everything went well, I had a great match. It's marvellous to be in the semifinals," said 31-year-old Waldner, the most sucessful player of the modern era.
His semifinal opponent China's Yan Sen was a 21-19 19-21 21-13 21-19 victor over Chinese-born He Zhi Wan of Spain.

Seven of the eight women's quarter-finalists were Chinese and four of them reached the semifinal with the last western player, European champion Nicole Struss of Germany, going down to joint ninth seed Wu Na 21-16 21-13 21-18.
World and Olympic champion Deng Yaping defeated Wong Ching 21-14 21-15 19-21 21-10 to earn a clash with joint third seed Li Ju, who beat Qiao Yunping 21-12 21-17 21-16.
Wu Na will battle for a place in the final against Wang Nan, a 21-18 22-20 18-21 21-9 winner over Cheng Hongxia.
